definitions.def: to make something known to many people widely
real and genuine, not fake or copied
a strong dedication to a cause or activity
the state of being known to the public, often for promotion
a pretense or false display meant to deceive

grammar_choice.en_template: {{1:Realising/Realised}} the benefits of differentiation, some brands broadcast their social purpose {{2:before/after}} they do much actual good.

explain: 주절 주어(some brands)와 능동 관계인 분사구문 → 현재분사 Realising.

grammar_choice.en_template: Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than {{1:embracing/embrace}} the purpose {{2:itself/themselves}}.

explain: rather than + 동명사 — 앞의 using과 병렬, embracing.
강조하는 대상 the purpose(단수) → 재귀대명사 itself.

grammar_choice.en_template: Making a real difference with social problems {{1:is/are}} hard enough; to succeed, it has to {{2:follow/be followed}} from an authentic, company-wide commitment to the purpose.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 사회 문제로 실제 변화를 만드는 것은 그 자체로 충분히 어렵다. 성공하려면 그것은 진정한, 회사 전체 차원의 목적에 대한 헌신에서 나와야 한다.
explain: 동명사 주어 Making ... 은 단수 취급 → is.
follow from(~에서 비롯되다)은 자동사 표현 — 수동태 불가, 능동 follow.

grammar_choice.en_template: We end up with {{1:what/that}} Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just furthers the charade of elites {{2:disrupting/disrupted}} the old order without giving much back".

explain: 선행사를 포함하고 describes의 목적어가 빠진 절 → 관계대명사 what.
elites가 능동으로 질서를 뒤흔드는 관계 → 현재분사 disrupting.

grammar_choice.en_template: Purpose-washing brands {{1:gain/gains}} one of the benefits of social purpose, differentiation, but only {{2:for/during}} a short while.

jumble.answer: Realising the benefits of differentiation, some brands broadcast their social purpose before they do much actual good.
Their marketers are using social purpose to boost the brand's reputation, rather than embracing the purpose itself.
Making a real difference with social problems is hard enough; to succeed, it has to follow from an authentic, company-wide commitment to the purpose.
Otherwise the mission is just window-dressing, or what we call "purpose-washing" — similar to green-washing, where purpose-driven activities serve mainly for publicity purposes.
We end up with what Anand Giridhardas describes in Winners Take All: "social purpose that just furthers the charade of elites disrupting the old order without giving much back".
Purpose-washing brands gain one of the benefits of social purpose, differentiation, but only for a short while.
They lose out on positioning for future markets, and they might even make employees feel worse about working for them.
